Media & description guide

You’re already welcome here—borrow language at your pace; nothing here grades your wording.

Five ways to describe Today’s Daily Battle, written like the porch itself: headline, about box, directory listing, fuller write-up, and founder voice.

Open the site About Story

Ready-to-use versions

1 sentence pitch 
Today's Daily Battle is a quiet, ad-free KJV porch where anyone can meet God through today's verse, a simple search, short plans, prayer, and notes that stay on this device.
Short blurb 
Today's Daily Battle is a calm, privacy-respecting KJV companion for hard weeks and ordinary Tuesdays. Today's verse, a search by feeling or question, short reading plans, prayer, and family pages — no ads, no account required. Verses, notes, and prayers stay on your device unless you choose to sign in.
Directory / press blurb 
Today's Daily Battle is a quiet King James porch, not a noisy Christian app. No ads, no signup wall, no streak to protect. It opens with today's verse, a search by feeling or a plain question, short reading plans, prayer, family pages, and a full KJV reader that still works after the first visit. Notes stay on your device unless you choose to sign in. Built from a hospital season and still used daily by the person who made it. You do not have to give. You do not have to be mid-battle to belong.
Full description 
Today's Daily Battle (todaysdailybattle.com) is a calm, ad-free King James porch. It is for anxiety, grief, fear, parenting, hope, and ordinary Tuesdays. There are no ads and no account required to open the Word. The site starts with today's verse, a search by feeling or question, short plans, prayer, family pages, and a full KJV reader that works on a phone and keeps working offline after the first visit. Notes stay on the device unless someone chooses to sign in. Built from a hospital season and still used every day by the person who made it. Giving is optional, with no suggested amount. The Word is never locked.
Founder voice 
The site was born in my own hospital-room pain when I needed plain KJV that met me where I was—no lectures, no polished production. I built what I could not find and still use it every day. It quietly continues the work of my father, Evangelist Thomas W. Barnard, who spent decades pointing people to the KJV and the hope of Jesus. I’m not a preacher. I’m a regular guy who needs the KJV the same way you do—on heavy days, quiet ones, and days you cannot name.

Deeper context (press, partners, directories)

Today’s Daily Battle is a solo-built, ad-free KJV porch. Anyone can walk in. Everything stays simple, private, and Scripture-centered on purpose.

What this is (longer read) 
Today's Daily Battle (todaysdailybattle.com) is a quiet, solo-built ministry around the public-domain King James Version. It is an ad-free porch for anxiety, grief, fear, parenting, hope, family life, and ordinary Tuesdays. The promise is small: one verse, a prayer if you want it, one next step. Tools keep working offline after the first visit. Notes stay on your device unless you choose to sign in.

"God's University of Life" is a gentle name, not a rebrand. The KJV is the textbook. The Holy Spirit is the Teacher. There are no grades and no finish line. The site is for hard hours and quiet ones. It is not a content farm. Built in West Tennessee from a hospital season, and still used daily. Binding privacy and security detail live on those pages.

X: @todaysdailybattle. Contact: support@todaysdailybattle.com. The Word stays free. If someone wants to help, they choose the amount. English KJV is the default. Small and human-scale on purpose.

Maintainers: a fuller deep dive (domain verify notes, streak nuance, doc links) lives in the repo at docs/MINISTRY-DEEP-DIVE-2026-04.md and is not published as its own page.

Best-use notes

  • Use the 1 sentence pitch for a short intro or a quick reply.
  • Use the short blurb for about boxes and short listings.
  • Use the directory / press blurb for newsletters, directories, or a mention.
  • Use the full description when someone wants the whole shape of the porch in one place.
  • Use the founder voice when it should sound like Brandon, not an institution.
  • Use the longer partner read for press kits and anyone who needs the whole posture—still calm, not a pitch.
